question: Approximate Zillow's Free Cash Flow as CFO - Capex. What was the trend of FCF margin from FY2022 to FY2024?
answer:
2024: 12.7%
2023: 11.3%
2022: 24.8%

FCF margin has declined substantially since 2022 and seems to have settled into a new normal of low teens percent.

model_answer:
Using **FCF = cash flow from operations − capital expenditures** and dividing by total revenue:

| Fiscal year | CFO | Capex | FCF | Revenue | **FCF margin** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2022 | $4.504B | $0.115B | **$4.389B** | $1.958B | **~224%** |
| 2023 | $0.354B | $0.135B | **$0.219B** | $1.945B | **~11.3%** |
| 2024 | $0.428B | $0.143B | **$0.285B** | $2.236B | **~12.7%** |

**Trend:** FCF margin fell dramatically from **~224% in FY2022 to ~11.3% in FY2023**, then improved modestly to **~12.7% in FY2024**.

The key caveat is that FY2022 is not a clean comparison: Zillow’s 2022 operating cash flow was inflated by roughly **$3.9B of inventory reduction** as it wound down its iBuying/Zillow Offers inventory. So the 2022 FCF margin was a liquidation-driven anomaly. Excluding that distortion, Zillow’s normalized FCF margin was roughly **low-double-digits**, and it expanded slightly in 2024 as revenue grew ~15% and CFO grew ~21%, while capex rose only ~6%.

Sources: Zillow FY2024 results and 2024 Form 10-K; cash-flow figures also summarized by [StockAnalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/z/financials/cash-flow-statement/).
judge_reason: 2022 FCF margin is ~224% instead of 24.8%, triggering contradiction, despite meeting 2023/2024 and trend checks.
